findings.defect: "The class ... is closed under def:damping, which multiplies every d^v by a positive scalar, so the reduction of thm:stopping-transform keeps the hypothesis" is FALSE: def:damping replaces EVERY edge by a chain, so a first-passage entry is reweighted by (1-beta)^{path length}, which is not a common scalar when targets sit at different depths.
findings.evidence: Explicit counterexample, exact rational arithmetic (t_signdef.py). G: v(max)->(B,A), w1(max)->(t1,t0), w2(max)->(t0,t1), A(avg)->(a1,w2), a1(avg)->(w1,w1), B(avg)->(w1,b1), b1(avg)->(w2,t0). G is stopping and sign-definite: d^v|_C = (0,0,-1/4) at v, 0 at w1,w2. Its damping G_m (def:damping, every edge replaced by a chain of m average vertices) has d^v|_C = (0, 1/16, -3/32) at m=1, (0, 9/128, -45/256) at m=2, (0, 49/1024, -441/2048) at m=3, (0, 225/8192, -3825/16384) at m=4 -- both signs present, so G_m is NOT sign-definite for any m tested. Hence the class is not closed under damping and thm:stopping-transform does not preserve the hypothesis.

findings.defect: The title ("an improving single-switch rule") and the statement ("consecutive profiles differing in one coordinate, every step is an improving single switch") are contradicted by the proposition's own proof, which concludes the opposite; and the statement's parenthetical repair is false.
findings.evidence: Statement l.8294-8296: 'consecutive profiles differing in one coordinate, every step is an improving single switch'. Proof l.8316-8320: 'several may flip at one breakpoint, so the path is a multi-switch improving rule (the route's auditor: 77 of 446 steps on random one-player games flip two or more coordinates ...)'. The statement's parenthetical l.8284-8285 'if two breakpoints coincide, delete the intermediate profile and the statement is unchanged' is false: after the deletion the step flips two coordinates. The single-switch reading is repeated in rem:bias-gap (l.8481-8483) and in the summary (l.16012-16013); the distinction is load-bearing, thm:switch-count bounding single-switch rules by N2^a and multi-switch ones only by N4^a.

findings.defect: The "more generally" clause and the superadditivity/Fekete conclusions drop the NONDEGENERACY hypothesis that lem:balance and thm:stack both require, while h*_1 is defined over games with ties allowed; so h*_1(m_1+m_2+1) >= h*_1(m_1)+h*_1(m_2) and the Fekete limit statement are not established.
findings.evidence: lem:balance (l.7358-7362) hypothesis: 'Let G_0 be a nondegenerate one-player normal form ... and gaps g_min := min|A_{b,1}-A_{b,0}| > 0'; thm:stack (l.7390-7391): 'Let \widehat G be a balanced nondegenerate one-player normal form'. With a tied block g_min=0 and lem:balance's condition 0<varsigma<(1-rho)^2 mu g_min/4 is vacuous. cor:stack-family l.7488-7490 states the general clause for 'a one-player normal form', with no nondegeneracy, and l.7492-7495 draws 'By Fekete's lemma the limit lim_m h*_1(m)/m exists and equals sup_{m_0} h*_1(m_0)/(m_0+1)'. That Fekete argument needs superadditivity of h*_1 itself, i.e. of the tie-allowing ceiling, which the construction does not deliver. (h*_1(7k)>=12k is unaffected and I confirmed ST(1) from the game file: 734 vertices, 7 Max, no tied incidence, USO, acyclic, BA height 12.)

findings.defect: "the one-player row is unbounded in ratio to the trivial one" overstates cor:stack-family, which gives only the constant factor 12/7, and is contradicted inside the same sentence by the Fekete cap and by the body's own wording.
findings.evidence: l.226-230: 'the one-player row is unbounded in ratio to the trivial one: stacking copies of a block behind a freezing bias gives one-player games with 7k Max vertices and runs of length 12k, a construction that Fekete's lemma caps at its best block'. The body, rem:stack-measured (l.7534-7536), says correctly: 'the first family of one-player stopping SSGs whose all-switches run exceeds |Vmax| by a CONSTANT FACTOR'. h*_1(m)/m >= 12/7 is a constant, not an unbounded ratio.

findings.defect: The acyclicity step is invalid as written: the union of the two acyclic inner orientations s and s(.+z) need not be acyclic, so "any directed cycle has constant inner vertex" does not follow from the sentence given.
findings.evidence: Proof text: 'Acyclicity: the inner coordinate moves only along edges of the acyclic s or of the acyclic s(\cdot\oplus z), so any directed cycle has constant inner vertex'. thm:blowup's own proof (l.5497-5499) argues correctly, using the extra fact that layer (0,0) is absorbing: 'No outer edge leaves layer (0,0), and inside it the orientation is the translate of s, so a directed cycle meeting (0,0) would lie in it'. The conclusion is true (I verified B_phi(s,z) is a USO and acyclic on all 9216 tall blow-ups of 3-cube seeds and on random samples); only the written justification is defective.

findings.defect: The clause "attained at the 2^{k+1} vertices ... over the 2^{k} vertices v of maximal height" presumes the number of maximal-height vertices of an AUSO is a power of two; it is not.
findings.evidence: Exhaustive over the 728 AUSOs of the 3-cube (t_bh.py): 32 of them have a number of maximal-height vertices that is not a power of two, e.g. s=(2,3,1,0,6,7,4,5) (USO, acyclic, sink 3) has heights (2,2,1,0,2,2,2,2), i.e. six vertices of maximal height. The identification of WHICH vertices attain 2h_u+2 is correct; only the cardinality is. (I verified the four displayed height formulas exactly over all 728 3-cube seeds and on the seeds of prop:hk-doubling-measured(b),(c) and prop:hkfive: no mismatch.)

findings.defect: "The same holds for B(s,z) with an arbitrary z, with h(o+z) in place of h_u" is true of the four displayed formulas but false of the preceding "In particular the height of B(s) is exactly 2h_u+2" clause.
findings.evidence: With z=0 the formulas give H(1,1,v)=h(v)+2+h(o)=h(v)+2, so the height of B(s,0) is h_s+2, not 2*h(o+0)+2=2. The general height is h_s+2+h(o+z), which equals 2h_u+2 only when u=o+z has maximal height -- which is exactly the hypothesis of thm:blowup and what prop:blowup-readout(b) then says ('with equality when u has maximal height').

findings.defect: "Admissibility is a real restriction here: it forbids directed cycles through calls" is false; admissibility (H stopping when calls are read as controlled) forbids only cycles inside the controlled-plus-call induced subgraph, and the conclusion drawn from it is therefore wrong too.
findings.evidence: By lem:trapchar admissibility makes the subgraph induced on Vmax u Vmin u calls acyclic, not the whole graph. Counterexample: H with a call c->(x,t_0) and x in Vavg, x->(c,t_0). Reading c as controlled, the trap iteration gives the empty trap (x needs both c and t_0, t_0 excluded; then c has no successor in U), so H is admissible, and c -> x -> c is a directed cycle through the call: the composition replays G indefinitely. Hence the following sentence, 'a cyclic finite-state device reading a stream of plays is not a context in this sense, and the bound says nothing about it', is also wrong -- such a device IS a context, and the amplification bound does cover it.

findings.defect: The proof asserts unconditionally that the interiors of the intervals I_S are disjoint, contradicting the statement's own nondegeneracy hypothesis and its explicit degenerate counterexample.
findings.evidence: Proof l.8233-8235: 'Uniqueness in (a) makes the interiors of the I_S disjoint with union [0,\infty), so each S occurs on one interval only.' Statement l.8207-8212: 'when the homotopy is NONDEGENERATE --- no two distinct S feasible on a common interval of positive length, WHICH FAILS on an explicit 25-vertex one-player game of the route's auditor --- they meet only in endpoints'. Uniqueness of the LCP solution does not make the SUPPORTS unique when a complementary pair vanishes simultaneously.

findings.defect: The rewritten preamble sentence "an improving switch cannot gain less than 2^{-a}" is still not right: the gain compares coordinates of two DIFFERENT value vectors, whose denominators may differ, and is only bounded below by 4^{-a}.

verdict:
NOT SOUND: seven majors and eleven minors survive. The majors are (1) rem:four-ceilings' new inequality h*_1 <= h*_LP <= h*_HK, which prop:oneplayer-lp does not give because h*_1 is defined with ties allowed and which the manuscript elsewhere calls open; (2) rem:signdef's false closure of the sign-definite class under def:damping, refuted here by an explicit 9-vertex game in exact arithmetic; (3) prop:bias-one-improving, whose "improving single-switch rule" statement and title are contradicted by its own proof ("multi-switch"); (4) the summary's "no named family ... costs it more than 2|C| switches", contradicted by prop:bias-witnesses (HAM_3 verified here: 7 breakpoints at |C|=3); (5) cor:stack-family's superadditivity/Fekete clauses, which drop the nondegeneracy hypothesis of lem:balance and thm:stack; (6) the abstract's "unbounded in ratio to the trivial one", which the body's own constant factor 12/7 and Fekete cap contradict; (7) the now-false "ties the best Holt-Klee height known there" at l.6767, made false by round 16's own prop:hk-records.
